title: Signal engine orchestration — non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #27 (signal-engine-orchestration), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: analyse() calls evaluate_wave(daily_ohlcv, tide) once directly for today's `wave`, then _wave_showed_state() calls evaluate_wave() again up to 5 times per target state (once for OVERSOLD_PULLBACK, once for OVERBOUGHT_RALLY) -- up to 11 total evaluate_wave() calls per analyse() invocation, each re-deriving the full Stochastic Oscillator/Force Index/rolling-std computations from scratch over its slice. Confirmed via code-review (medium effort) on this PR's diff: evaluate_wave's result never depends on target_state, and since evaluate_wave can only ever produce OVERSOLD_PULLBACK when tide==BULLISH or OVERBOUGHT_RALLY when tide==BEARISH (never both for a given tide), one of the two _wave_showed_state calls is guaranteed to do 5 fully wasted evaluate_wave invocations on every single analyse() call, and the direct `wave` computation duplicates the lookback loop's final (full-length) iteration again on top of that. Not a correctness issue on current single-ticker, on-demand-analysis data sizes (~2-3x cost multiplier on analyse(), which runs once per held/watched ticker), but worth refactoring to compute each lookback bar's wave state once (cache per slice-length, or skip the loop whose target_state can never match the current tide) and check against a single pass instead of two independent loops.

evaluate_impulse(daily_ohlcv) (app/signals/impulse.py, pre-existing) internally computes ema(daily_close, 13) and macd_histogram(daily_close) but only returns the derived GREEN/RED/BLUE color, discarding the series. analyse() then separately recomputes ema(daily_close, 13) and macd_components(daily_close).histogram on the same daily_close for the `indicators` dict this PR added. Both computations produce identical values (same inputs, same functions) but run twice with no sharing -- correctness is unaffected (indicators is independent of evaluate_impulse's return value) but it's real duplicated work introduced by this PR now that analyse() needs those series for a second purpose. Consider having evaluate_impulse optionally accept/return the underlying EMA(13)/MACD-Histogram series (or restructure so engine.py computes them once and passes them to both evaluate_impulse and the indicators dict) next time impulse.py or engine.py is touched.
